newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds steady after losses, eye U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds steady after losses, eye U.S. data.

text.p: Irish government bonds steadied in gentle afternoon trade on Wednesday after mild morning losses, as the market looked ahead to a mixed bag of inflationary data in the U.S. on Thursday, dealers said.
"Irish bonds dropped in morning trade but we are still out performing UK gilts which are shakey ahead of the U.S. figures tomorrow," one dealer said.
Thursday sees the release of U.S. retail prices, consumer prices, jobless claims and money supply figures.
By 1549 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 was down 13p at 106.22 to yield 6.08 percent.
The eight percent bond due 2006 slipped 15p from Tuesday's close at 107.80 to yield 6.76 percent.
Earlier, UK September average earnings rose 4.0 percent, in line with expectations, while the jobless rate fell to 7.2 percent in October against forecasts of 7.3 percent.
UK unit wage costs were up 5.2 percent in the three months to September as against an expected rise of 4.5 percent. October unemployment was down 40,800 against a predicted fall of 25,000.
Meantime, minutes from the October 23 UK monetary meeting showed Bank of England governor Eddie George arguing that interest rates might have to rise above six percent.
"Recent market conditions have helped the Irish market to cheapen up marginally with German bunds," one dealer said.
"In the 10-year spread with Germany, Ireland is holding out at 100 basis points," he added.
"The sterling/punt exchange rate situation has improved somewhat and we will be expecting better sentiment to feed through to the bond market," one dealer said.
Dealers said they would be looking for Thursday's U.S. data to reaffirm the view that the domestic inflationary climate was still stable.
